logo, slash and two-line breadcrumb top-left; rounded status pill top-right

standard name repeated in a left label column outside the folders
bottom row in deep navy folders, cropped at the bottom edge

paper luggage tag with metal eyelet and ring for one standard
torn paper slip for a proof item
binder clip and paper clip holding documents

regular sans on paper notes, slightly larger than body
light sans breadcrumb with slash separator

paper luggage tag with metal eyelet
t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section seen straight-on from above, on a warm limestone surface with a soft diagonal window-light shadow. A small header strip with logo and breadcrumb, then four uppercase column headers. Each table row is a photo-real manila file folder laid across the width, staggered and overlapping, carrying <CONTENT> on index cards, a luggage tag with metal eyelet, a torn paper slip and a stamped revision box, held by binder and paper clips. A plain label column at left repeats each row name. The last rows are deep navy folders with navy label chips. Paper grain, soft shadows, tactile and archival.
signature_idea: The table is built out of stacked manila folders, so each standard literally is a file whose proof is clipped, tagged and stamped onto it.
strengths: metaphor is now structural: every row is its folder, which reads as 'filed evidence' for QA readers
column headers keep the table scannable despite the props
navy chips give a restrained emphasis in brand colour
limestone and navy palette with no red accent
warm, human contrast to the blueprint pages could work as one memorable moment
weaknesses: very busy; props, shadows and paper textures compete with the content
photo-real collage is hard to build responsively and off the line-drawing system
row 2 shows a stray '2' instead of a label, labels are duplicated inside and outside folders
no mono figures, rounded pill badge breaks square corners
brand_fit_why: Palette (limestone, navy, steel-grey ink) is on-brand and the dossier idea suits pharma QA, but the cluttered photo-real collage, missing mono figures and rounded pill drift from the precise, calm, square line-drawing language.
